newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon central bank takes up most of MEA shares.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon central bank takes up most of MEA shares.

text.p: Lebanon's Middle East Airlines (MEA) said on Saturday that the central bank has taken up most of the $100 million worth of shares in a capital increase agreed in July to pay for the ailing airliner's debt.

MEA chairman Khaled Salam told a news conference after a shareholders' meeting that the Bank of Lebanon, which covers MEA's $100 million debt, took up 90 percent of the shares as most other shareholders did not participate.
In July, MEA launched an operation to increase its capital by $225 million, to rehabilitate the airline, upgrade its 14-plane fleet and pay its debts.

Shareholders have agreed to carry out a $100 million debt for equity swap as the first stage of the increase and MEA last month invited shareholders to subscribe. The central bank was to take up shares not taken up by other shareholders.
Salam said MEA employees have subscribed to two percent of the shares.

But Air France, which held 28.5 percent of MEA, and Intra Investent Company, a holding company owned by the Lebanese government and the Kuwait and Qatari governments and investors which owned 62.5 percent of MEA, did not take part, he added.

"Air France's shareholding has become 0.5 percent because under the deal it will sell its shares to the central bank. As for Intra, it is about nine percent now while for the Bank of Lebanon, it is 90 percent," Salam said.
MEA flourished before the 1975-90 Lebanese civil war but the fighting and the devaluation of the Lebanese pound have reduced its 150 million pound capital to $96,000 before the last capital increase.

Salam said that an additional increase of $125 million in capital will be agreed at a shareholders meeting on October 11. MEA officials have said that the $125 million will come from cash contribution from shareholders.
Salam said MEA was in negotiations to lease four new Airbus planes, which he hoped would join the fleet at the start of 1997.
"The atmosphere is very positive, because for the first time Middle East Airlines is out of intensive care and enters the stage of work," Salam added.
